meta.note: Curated from public sources (brand newsrooms, press coverage, ACSI, Axios Harris Poll 100, YouGov). AI-voice samples are authentic LLM outputs generated by Claude (Anthropic) on the date shown. Replace this file with a live API response of the same shape to make the tracker live — see assets/js/brand-tracker.js.

official.label: Official Voice
official.description: How the brand speaks for itself — campaigns, newsrooms, and executive statements (2024–2026).

consumer.label: Consumer Voice
consumer.description: How consumers rate and talk about the brand — satisfaction and reputation indices plus documented consumer reactions.

ai.label: AI-Generated Voice
ai.description: How an LLM describes and markets the brand — authentic model outputs, labeled with model and date.

official.summary: Athlete-first empowerment with a sharper edge: 2025's 'So Win' anthem — Nike's first Super Bowl ad in 27 years — put women athletes center stage.

samples.text: So Win.
samples.attribution: Brand anthem, Super Bowl LIX (voiced by Doechii, feat. Caitlin Clark, Sha'Carri Richardson, A'ja Wilson)

samples.text: No matter how hard you work, how much you prove or how many barriers you break, there will always be doubters. If you can't win in everyone's eyes, win in your own.
samples.attribution: Nicole Graham, Nike CMO, 'So Win' launch

consumer.summary: Satisfaction is slipping — ACSI down 5% and longtime fans question product quality — even as Nike still leads U.S. fashion purchase consideration.

samples.text: What used to be premium is no longer being made.
samples.attribution: Sneaker enthusiast on Nike's quality drift
samples.source: Marketplace, 'Can Nike win back its sneakerheads?'

samples.text: Recurring review themes: declining product quality, unhelpful customer service, refund difficulties.
samples.attribution: Dominant themes in nike.com reviews

ai.summary: The LLM frames Nike as the default performance brand with premium pricing; AI influencer-style content reproduces 'Just Do It' self-discipline tropes.

samples.text: Nike is the world's largest athletic footwear and apparel brand, known for performance innovation like its Air and ZoomX cushioning and for decades of culture-shaping marketing. It's a default choice for runners and sneaker enthusiasts alike, though it commands premium prices.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: 5am. Empty streets. Just me and my Pegasus. Some people chase sunrises — I outrun them. 🏃‍♀️ #JustDoIt
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: Superlative-led product marketing now organized around AI: the lineup-wide line is 'Built for Apple Intelligence.'

samples.text: Built for Apple Intelligence.
samples.attribution: Lineup-wide marketing line (updated from 'Hello, Apple Intelligence')

samples.text: These iPhone 17 Pro models are the most advanced Pro models we've ever created and this new iPhone lineup represents the biggest leap ever for iPhone.
samples.attribution: Tim Cook, CEO, iPhone 17 launch event

consumer.summary: Satisfaction stays at the top of the category, but the AI story isn't landing: most surveyed users say Apple Intelligence adds little value, and brand loyalty hit its lowest point since 2019.

samples.text: 73% of Apple Intelligence users say the AI features add little to no value; iPhone brand loyalty fell to 78.9%, the lowest since 2019.
samples.attribution: Survey of iPhone owners

samples.text: Consumer frustration mounted over the personalized-Siri delay to 2026 — internally, even Apple's Siri chief called the delays 'ugly' and 'embarrassing.'
samples.attribution: Coverage of Siri AI delays

ai.summary: The LLM presents Apple as the integrated-ecosystem benchmark with a privacy premium — notably warmer than current consumer chatter about its AI features.

samples.text: Apple designs premium consumer electronics — iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch — built around a tightly integrated ecosystem and a strong privacy stance. Its products carry high prices but consistently rank at the top for customer satisfaction and resale value.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: Typed this on my Mac, timed my run with my Watch, and never once worried who's reading my texts. The ecosystem really is the flex. 🍎
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: The 'Real Magic' platform continues, now executed with AI: the 2025 holiday campaign paired 'Holidays Are Coming' nostalgia with AI-generated storytelling.

samples.text: Real Magic — saluting people around the world whose generous acts of goodwill help make Christmas the most special time of year.
samples.attribution: Islam ElDessouky, Global VP Creative Strategy & Content, on the AI-powered 'Givers of the Season' holiday campaign

consumer.summary: Still the satisfaction leader among soft-drink makers, but 2025 showed how fast sentiment can move: a false viral video triggered a boycott and a ~4% North America sales dip.

samples.text: Volume was impacted by weakening consumer sentiment as the quarter progressed, particularly among Hispanic consumers.
samples.attribution: James Quincey, CEO, on the fallout from a false viral video (debunked by Reuters) that triggered a boycott

samples.text: In company surveys, ~75% of Hispanic consumers reported scaling back on eating out and social gatherings, citing immigration-crackdown and inflation worries.
samples.attribution: Consumer-survey coverage

ai.summary: The LLM treats Coca-Cola as the canonical emotional-branding case and mirrors its nostalgia register — omitting the sentiment volatility visible in consumer data.

samples.text: Coca-Cola is the world's most recognized soft-drink brand, over 130 years old, built on consistent taste and emotionally resonant marketing about happiness and togetherness. Its portfolio now spans zero-sugar variants, waters, and juices as consumers shift away from sugary sodas.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: Golden hour picnic, ice-cold Coke Zero in hand. Some classics never need a rebrand. ✨🥤
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: 'i'm lovin' it' remains the global slogan (since 2003); 2025's flagship move was pure nostalgia — reviving McDonaldland and its characters after 20+ years.

samples.text: Experience the Magic of McDonaldland.
samples.attribution: McDonaldland revival campaign — return of Ronald McDonald, Grimace, Hamburglar and Mayor McCheese

samples.text: Over the past few years we've seen how fans flock to our characters, everyone from Grimace to the Hamburglar. There's an entire magical world of McDonaldland filled with characters, places and lore.
samples.attribution: Jennifer 'JJ' Healan, VP of U.S. Marketing, Brand, Content and Culture

consumer.summary: Last place among major fast-food chains in customer satisfaction, with price anger as the defining story — the viral $18 Big Mac meal forced an open letter from McDonald's US president and a $5 value meal.

samples.text: Maybe this went up way too fast.
samples.attribution: Consumer reaction to the viral $18 Big Mac meal

samples.text: The $18 Big Mac combo 'sparked a revolt against high prices' — strong enough that McDonald's US president published an open letter calling it an exception (average Big Mac: $5.29, +20.5% since 2019).
samples.attribution: Coverage of consumer price backlash

ai.summary: The LLM leads with scale and consistency, and — unlike its treatment of most brands — spontaneously surfaces the price criticism consumers voice.

samples.text: McDonald's is the world's largest fast-food chain, serving roughly 70 million customers daily on a model of speed, consistency, and value. Its app-driven loyalty program is among the most used in retail, even as it fields criticism over nutrition and rising menu prices.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: It's giving 3am fries energy and I will not apologize. The app deals are actually unmatched rn. 🍟
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: A brand in deliberate reset: the 'Back to Starbucks' strategy reintroduced the chain with 'Not My Name' and the Super Bowl-window spot 'Hello Again.'

samples.text: Hello again. The Starbucks you love is ready.
samples.attribution: 'Hello Again' spot (aired around Super Bowl LIX), following the 'Not My Name' campaign launch

samples.text: We must reestablish ourselves as the community coffeehouse. Starbucks has always been a place where people come together.
samples.attribution: Brian Niccol, Chairman & CEO, 'Back to Starbucks' remarks

consumer.summary: Solid satisfaction scores mask strain: reputation fell sharply in 2025, and only about half of customers consider Starbucks affordable — the lowest of the big U.S. coffee chains.

samples.text: Only 51% of customers agree Starbucks is affordable — the lowest of the seven largest U.S. coffee chains (Dunkin': 74%, Tim Hortons: 79%).
samples.attribution: Affordability survey coverage

samples.text: Counter-signal: under the turnaround, customer-connection scores are up and complaints down quarter-over-quarter.
samples.attribution: Customer-experience coverage

ai.summary: The LLM already narrates the turnaround: it reproduces the 'third place' positioning while citing the union disputes and price complaints the brand is trying to move past.

samples.text: Starbucks is the world's largest coffeehouse chain, positioned as a 'third place' between home and work, with a powerhouse mobile app and rewards program. Recent years brought union disputes and complaints about wait times and prices, which its 'Back to Starbucks' turnaround plan is trying to address.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: Rainy Tuesday, window seat, iced brown sugar oatmilk shaken espresso. My personality? Yes. ☕
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: No ad campaigns — Tesla's flagship communication is Master Plan Part IV, which broadens the mission from 'sustainable energy' to 'sustainable abundance.'

samples.text: The tools we are going to develop will help us build the kind of world that we've always dreamed of — a world of sustainable abundance — by redefining the fundamental building blocks of labor, mobility and energy at scale and for all.
samples.attribution: Master Plan Part IV, closing line

consumer.summary: The starkest voice gap in the tracker: product satisfaction stays high (ACSI 81) while brand reputation collapsed — #95 of 100 in the Harris Poll, down from #8 in 2021, with YouGov impressions at a nine-year low.

samples.text: I bought this before we knew Elon was crazy.
samples.attribution: Best-selling bumper sticker among Tesla owners — the defining consumer-sentiment artifact of 2025

samples.text: A Yale study estimated Musk's political activity cost Tesla roughly 1–1.26 million U.S. sales (Oct 2022–Apr 2025), with Democratic buyers leaving faster than Republican buyers arrived.
samples.attribution: Academic estimate of the brand-politics effect

ai.summary: The LLM hedges: it credits Tesla with forcing the industry electric while explicitly flagging the brand as 'unusually polarizing' — closer to consumer reality than to Tesla's own voice.

samples.text: Tesla is the EV maker that forced the auto industry electric, known for software-first cars, over-the-air updates, and its Supercharger network. Its brand is unusually polarizing — product loyalty runs deep while its CEO's public profile divides consumers.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: Charged at home overnight, autopiloted through traffic, zero gas stations since 2024. Living in the future is a choice. ⚡
samples.attribution: Prompt: lifestyle-influencer post

official.summary: Product-led rather than tagline-led: the 2026 flagship was a Super Bowl LX spot selling Alexa+ by joking about AI paranoia, atop the standing 'customer obsession' mission.

samples.text: Chris Hemsworth thinks Alexa+ is scary good.
samples.attribution: Super Bowl LX spot for Alexa+, Amazon's generative-AI assistant, feat. Chris Hemsworth and Elsa Pataky

samples.text: Amazon strives to be Earth's most customer-centric company, Earth's best employer, and Earth's safest place to work.
samples.attribution: Standing mission statement on all Amazon press releases

consumer.summary: Among the most satisfied customer bases in retail — top of online retail in ACSI and YouGov's 'most persuasive' U.S. brand — with a persistent complaint tail about deliveries and AI-only customer service.

samples.text: Recurring review themes: packages arriving days later than advertised, deliveries marked complete but missing, and frustration that customer service 'uses AI and not real people.'
samples.attribution: Dominant themes in amazon.com reviews (note: review platforms skew toward complainants)

samples.text: On the positive side, Amazon keeps strengthening on value, convenience, and consideration metrics among U.S. consumers.
samples.attribution: Brand-health analysis

ai.summary: The LLM pairs the convenience story with the counterfeit/labor caveats — a more hedged portrait than Amazon's own voice, and close to the consumer split.

samples.text: Amazon is the dominant e-commerce and cloud-computing company, synonymous with fast Prime delivery and near-endless selection. Consumers rate its convenience highly while raising concerns about counterfeit listings, review authenticity, and labor practices.
samples.attribution: Prompt: describe the brand to a consumer

samples.text: Ordered a tripod at midnight, filming with it by noon. Prime really said 'instant gratification, but make it logistics.' 📦
